mainTopic: Testing and defending the claim of the תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל that there are exactly eighteen טרפות
overview: Our משנה lists many טרפות and then gives a general rule (זה הכלל) that covers anything it left out. The תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל, however, says there are exactly eighteen טרפות and no more. The גמרא tests this closed count against cases that seem to be missing from it. Some cases drop out because this תנא follows a sage who calls the animal kosher: a leg cut off above the joint (like רבי שמעון בן אלעזר) and an animal whose hide was stripped off (like רבי מאיר). Other cases fit by reshuffling the list: the המסס and בית הכוסות count as one to make room for a missing vertebra, and the gallbladder comes out so the shriveled lung can go in. Then the גמרא raises seven later rulings of אמוראים and answers that all eight perforated organs count as one, which frees seven places. The amud ends by attacking that answer. The two severed cases should then also count as one, and the perforated spleen is itself a perforation, so the list falls two short of eighteen.

steps.title: How can there be only eighteen טרפות if a cut-off leg is also a טרפה?
steps.stepSummary: Our משנה's list is open-ended because of its general rule. רבי ישמעאל's school says exactly eighteen, so the גמרא asks where the case of a leg cut off above the joint fits.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our תנא is fine: whatever he listed, he listed, and whatever he left out is covered by 'This is the principle.' But רבי ישמעאל's school said 'eighteen טרפות, and no more.' Isn't there also an animal whose legs were cut off from the joint and up, which is a טרפה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the claim of the תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל that there are exactly eighteen טרפות. It points to a case that is not on his list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה has no problem with missing cases, because its general rule (זה הכלל) picks up anything it did not list. רבי ישמעאל's school gave a closed number, so any טרפה outside the eighteen breaks the count. The leg cut off above the joint (taught in a later משנה) seems to be exactly such a case.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with a fatal defect, forbidden to eat even after proper שחיטה
'Granted…': this view is fine, but the other one has a problem
'This is the principle': the general rule in our משנה that covers cases it did not list
That which he left out
The leg joint (knee area)

steps.confusionAlert: Our משנה is not being questioned here. Only the school of רבי ישמעאל has a problem, because only they gave a fixed number with 'no more.'

phrases.english: Granted, according to the tanna of our mishna,
what he taught, he taught, and what he left out
comes under 'This is the principle,'
phrases.notes: This points to the general rule at the end of our משנה, which catches any case not listed.

phrases.english: but according to the tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר: שְׁמוֹנֶה עֶשְׂרֵה טְרֵפוֹת וְתוּ לֵיכָּא,
phrases.english: who said: eighteen tereifot, and there are no more,
but isn't there an animal
whose legs were cut off
from the joint and above, which is a tereifa?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְתַנָּא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל דְּאָמַר: שְׁמוֹנֶה עֶשְׂרֵה טְרֵפוֹת וְתוּ לֵיכָּא, וְהָא אִיכָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the challenge to the closed count of eighteen
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim of the תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל that there are exactly eighteen טרפות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A leg cut off above the joint is a טרפה but is not on the list of eighteen, so the closed count seems wrong.

steps.title: He holds like רבי שמעון בן אלעזר that the animal can survive
steps.stepSummary: First answer: the תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, who says the cut leg can be sealed by burning and the animal can live.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds like רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, who said: the animal can be cauterized and live.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי ישמעאל's school does not count the cut-off leg as a טרפה. They follow רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, who says the animal can heal and live.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that a טרפה is an animal that cannot survive. If the wound can be burned closed and the animal lives, it would not be a טרפה, so it does not belong on the list.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds like (a certain sage's view)
To be cauterized: the wound is sealed by burning
To live, to survive

phrases.aramaic: סָבַר לֵיהּ כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר,
phrases.english: He holds like Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar,
who says: it can be cauterized and live.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָבַר לֵיהּ כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about the cut-off leg
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the view to a sage who holds the case is not a טרפה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The cut-off leg seemed to be a טרפה missing from the list
steps.terutzMaskana: Because the animal can survive, this תנא does not count it as a טרפה

steps.title: Survival does not matter for this תנא, since he holds a טרפה can live
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the first answer. רבי ישמעאל's school holds that a טרפה can live, so the fact that the animal survives does not prove it is kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even if it can be cauterized and live, whose view are we discussing? The view of רבי ישמעאל's school. But רבי ישמעאל's school holds that a טרפה can live!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave. The reason 'it can live' does not work for this particular תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer assumed that 'can survive' means 'not a טרפה.' But the תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל holds that a טרפה can live (טרפה חיה). For him, survival tells us nothing about whether the animal is a טרפה, so the answer fails.

keyTerms.meaning: Even though
'According to whom is this said?': whose view are we talking about?
The view that a טרפה animal is able to survive

steps.confusionAlert: There are two different ideas of טרפה here. Some hold a טרפה is an animal that will die; this תנא holds a טרפה can live. Under his view, 'it survives' cannot be the reason it is kosher.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דִּיכוֹלָה לִיכּוֹוֹת וְלִחְיוֹת,
phrases.english: Even though it can be cauterized and live,
according to whom is this being said?
phrases.notes: He means: the question about the cut-off leg is being asked on this תנא's own view, so we must use his rules.

phrases.english: According to the tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael;

phrases.aramaic: תַּנָּא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל טְרֵפָה חַיָּה סְבִירָא לֵיהּ!
phrases.english: but the tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael holds that a tereifa can live!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף עַל גַּב דִּיכוֹלָה לִיכּוֹוֹת וְלִחְיוֹת, לְמַאן קָאָמַר?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reasoning of the previous answer
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason 'it can be cauterized and live' given in step 2
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This תנא holds a טרפה can live, so being able to live does not show the animal is not a טרפה.

steps.title: He holds like רבי שמעון בן אלעזר only that the animal is kosher
steps.stepSummary: Revised answer: the תנא agrees with רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's ruling that the animal is kosher, but not with his reason about survival.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he holds like רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, who said: 'It is kosher.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes its answer. This תנא follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's final ruling that the animal is כשרה, without using the 'it can live' reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling and the reason are now separated. The תנא accepts the result (the animal is kosher) for his own reasons. So the cut-off leg is still not a טרפה for him, and the count of eighteen holds.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Rather': drops the earlier answer and gives a new one
Kosher, permitted to eat

steps.whatToRemember: The cut-off leg is not on רבי ישמעאל's list because he holds, like רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, that such an animal is כשרה. He does not rely on the reason that it can survive.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר,
phrases.english: Rather, he holds like Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar,
who says: 'It is kosher.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer with a revised one
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adopting the sage's ruling without his reason
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The animal is kosher because it can survive
steps.terutzMaskana: The animal is kosher as a ruling, without depending on whether it can survive

steps.title: What about a missing vertebra in the spine?
steps.stepSummary: A new challenge: שמואל says a missing vertebra in the spine makes an animal a טרפה, and that case is not on the list of eighteen.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't there a missing piece of the spine? As we learned: how much counts as missing from the spine? בית שמאי say two vertebrae, and בית הלל say one vertebra. And רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: the same is true for טרפה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second case that seems to break the count of eighteen: an animal missing part of its spine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה about the spine is about a dead body and טומאה. שמואל adds that the same measure applies to טרפה, so by בית הלל even one missing vertebra makes an animal a טרפה. That is another טרפה missing from the closed list.

keyTerms.meaning: A missing part of the spine
A vertebra, one bone of the spine (plural: חוּלְיוֹת)
'And the same for טרפה': the same measure applies to an animal

phrases.english: But isn't there a deficiency in the spine?
As we learned: how much is a deficiency in the spine?
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in אהלות 2:3, about a dead person's spine and טומאה.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: two vertebrae,
and Beit Hillel say: one vertebra;
and Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
and so too with regard to a tereifa.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a second case against the closed count, after the first was answered
steps.kashyaTarget: The count of exactly eighteen טרפות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל rules that a missing vertebra makes an animal a טרפה, yet it is not one of the eighteen.

steps.title: Count the המסס and בית הכוסות as one, making room for the spine
steps.stepSummary: Answer: two stomach items that were counted separately should be counted as one. That frees one slot for the spine case, and the total stays eighteen.
steps.simpleTranslation: The המסס and the בית הכוסות, which you counted as two, count them as one. Take one out and put one in.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by adjusting how the list is counted. Two stomach parts become one item, and the spine case takes the open slot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The number eighteen does not change; the contents of the list are reorganized. A hole in the המסס and a hole in the בית הכוסות are treated as one kind of טרפה. That leaves room for the missing vertebra, so the count still works.

keyTerms.meaning: The omasum, one of the stomachs of an animal that chews its cud
The reticulum, another of the stomachs
'Take one out and put one in': swap one item on the list for another

steps.whatToRemember: The list of eighteen stays at eighteen: the המסס and בית הכוסות count as one item, and the missing vertebra in the spine fills the open place.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the count of eighteen is a fixed number, but how cases are grouped inside it can be adjusted to fit every known טרפה.

phrases.english: The omasum and the reticulum,
which you counted as two,
count them as one;
take one out and put one in.
phrases.notes: The one put in is the missing vertebra from the step before.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֶמְסֵס וּבֵית הַכּוֹסוֹת, דְּקָא חָשְׁבַתְּ לְהוּ בְּתַרְתֵּי, חַשְׁבִינְהוּ בַּחֲדָא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Recounting the list: joining two items to open a slot
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The list was already full with eighteen items, so the spine case did not fit
steps.terutzMaskana: המסס and בית הכוסות are one item, so the spine case fits and the total stays eighteen

steps.title: What about an animal whose hide was removed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why גלודה, an animal whose hide was stripped off, is missing from the list of eighteen טרפות.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is also the case of an animal whose hide was removed! Why isn't it counted?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises another case that seems to be a טרפה but is not on the list of eighteen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A later משנה lists גלודה as a טרפה. If it is a טרפה, the list of eighteen should include it, and then the count would be wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal whose hide was completely stripped off
But isn't there...? (a word that opens a challenge)

phrases.english: But isn't there the animal whose hide was removed?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the spine case was fitted into the count, the גמרא raises another case that seems to be missing.
steps.kashyaTarget: The completeness of the list of eighteen טרפות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: גלודה is taught as a טרפה, but it does not appear on the list.

steps.title: This list follows רבי מאיר, who says it is kosher
steps.stepSummary: The תנא holds like רבי מאיר, who rules that a גלודה is kosher, so it does not belong on the list.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds like רבי מאיר, who says it is kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this תנא simply does not consider גלודה a טרפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question about גלודה is a מחלוקת. Since this תנא follows רבי מאיר, who rules it kosher, there is nothing missing from the list.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds like... (follows the opinion of)
Rules it kosher (permitted)

phrases.english: He holds like רבי מאיר
who rules it kosher.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Places the תנא on one side of a מחלוקת
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every animal whose hide was removed is a טרפה, so it should be on the list.
steps.terutzMaskana: This תנא follows רבי מאיר, who says גלודה is kosher, so the list is still complete.

steps.title: What about a shriveled lung?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why חרותא, a shriveled lung, is not on the list.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is also the shriveled lung! Why isn't it counted?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more טרפה that seems to be missing from the eighteen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A shriveled lung makes an animal a טרפה, but it is not one of the eighteen. If the list is already full, there seems to be no room for it.

keyTerms.meaning: A shriveled, dried-up lung

phrases.english: But isn't there the shriveled lung?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another case that seems to be missing from the count.
steps.kashyaTarget: The completeness of the list of eighteen
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: חרותא is a טרפה but is not on the list.

steps.title: Remove the gallbladder and put the shriveled lung in its place
steps.stepSummary: A perforated gallbladder is a טרפה only according to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, so the תנא drops it from the list and counts חרותא instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: The gallbladder: who teaches that it is a טרפה? רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. So take out the gallbladder and put in the shriveled lung.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא swaps one item on the list for another, so the total stays eighteen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only one Sage, רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, holds that a perforated gallbladder is a טרפה. This תנא does not follow that single opinion, so he drops מרה. That frees a slot for חרותא.

keyTerms.meaning: The gallbladder
Take out
And put in

phrases.english: The gallbladder: who teaches it?
רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
Take out the gallbladder and put in the shriveled lung.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 9 by swapping one item for another.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Swaps one item for another to keep the count at eighteen
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The list already has eighteen items, including the gallbladder, so there is no room for חרותא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The gallbladder is only one Sage's view, so it comes out and חרותא goes in.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the same method as step 6: when a new case is raised, the count is kept at eighteen by freeing up a slot.

steps.title: Seven more טרפות from the אמוראים: the first three
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises seven later cases of טרפות that are not on the list. It begins with a dislocated hip bone, a diseased kidney, and a perforated spleen.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there are seven more rulings! רב מתנא said: if the head of the thigh bone slipped out of its socket, the animal is a טרפה. רכיש בר פפא said in the name of רב: if one kidney is diseased, it is a טרפה. And a משנה teaches that if the spleen was removed, the animal is kosher, and רב עוירא said in the name of רבא: that is only when it was removed, but if it was perforated, it is a טרפה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a big challenge, seven new טרפות at once, and starts listing them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is much harder than one missing case. Swapping one item cannot make room for seven. The first three come from אמוראים: a dislocated hip bone, one diseased kidney, and a perforated spleen.

keyTerms.meaning: Seven rulings (seven extra cases of טרפות)
The ball at the top of the thigh bone (the hip joint)
Kidney
Spleen
They only taught this when... (limits a ruling)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up removed and perforated. A spleen that was removed completely is kosher, but a spleen with a hole in it makes the animal a טרפה.

phrases.english: But aren't there seven rulings,
as רב מתנא said:
This head of the thigh bone
that slipped out of its place is a טרפה,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רָכִישׁ בַּר פָּפָּא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב:
phrases.english: and רכיש בר פפא said in the name of רב:
If it was diseased in one kidney, it is a טרפה,
and we learned: if the spleen was removed, it is kosher,
and רב עוירא said in the name of רבא:
They taught this only when it was removed,
but if it was perforated, it is a טרפה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Escalates from single missing cases to seven at once.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the list of eighteen is complete
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Seven טרפות taught by אמוראים are missing, too many to fix by swapping one item.

steps.title: Seven more טרפות: the four from שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The list of seven continues with four rulings of שמואל: the סימנים mostly torn loose, a rib torn out from its root, a skull mostly crushed, and most of the flesh covering the rumen torn.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of שמואל: if the סימנים were mostly torn loose, the animal is a טרפה. And רבה בר רב שילא said in the name of רב מתנא in the name of שמואל: if a rib was torn out from its root, it is a טרפה. So too a skull that was mostly crushed, and the flesh covering most of the rumen if most of it was torn: these are טרפה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes listing the seven extra טרפות. The next step answers this whole challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Together with step 11, this makes seven: three in step 11 and four here. All of them are rulings of אמוראים that do not appear on the list of eighteen, so the challenge is now fully laid out.

keyTerms.meaning: The windpipe and the food pipe, the two organs cut in שחיטה
Were torn loose (detached)
Rib
A skull that was crushed
The rumen, the animal's first stomach

steps.whatToRemember: The seven extra טרפות are: a dislocated hip bone, one diseased kidney, a perforated spleen, סימנים mostly torn loose, a rib torn from its root, a mostly crushed skull, and torn flesh over the rumen. The next step explains how the list of eighteen still holds up.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: And רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of שמואל:
סימנים that were torn loose for most of their length are a טרפה.
And רבה בר רב שילא said
in the name of רב מתנא, in the name of שמואל:
If a rib was torn out from its root, it is a טרפה,
and a skull that was mostly crushed,
and the flesh that covers most of the rumen,
if most of it was torn, it is a טרפה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the list of seven started in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The completeness of the list of eighteen
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Four more rulings of שמואל add to the missing טרפות, bringing the total to seven.

steps.title: All eight perforation cases count as one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the question about the seven missing cases. The תנא counts the eight 'perforated' cases as a single case, which frees up seven places in the count of eighteen for the seven new cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are eight cases of a perforated organ. The תנא counts them as one. So he took out seven and put in seven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from steps 11 and 12. It explains how seven new cases can fit into a list of eighteen without going over the number.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists eight separate kinds of perforated organs. If the תנא treats 'perforation' as one category, he only uses one slot for all eight. The seven slots this frees up go to the seven later cases, so the total stays at eighteen.

keyTerms.meaning: perforated (organs with a hole in them)
he counts them as one
he took out
he brought in, inserted

steps.confusionAlert: Nobody is saying the eight perforated organs stop being טרפה. All of them still make the animal a טרפה. The question is only how to count them toward the number eighteen.

phrases.english: The perforated cases are eight,
he counts them as one,
he took out seven, and brought in seven.
phrases.notes: The seven he brings in are the seven later cases listed in steps 11 and 12.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 11 and 12 about seven later טרפות missing from the list.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-counting: grouping several cases into one category to free up places in the list.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought each of the eight perforation cases took its own place in the count, so there was no room left for seven more.
steps.terutzMaskana: All perforations count as one item, leaving seven places for the seven new cases.

steps.title: Then the two severed cases should also count as one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back. If eight perforations count as one, then the two 'severed' cases should also count as one, and the list falls one short of eighteen.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the severed cases are also two. Count them as one too. Then the list is short by one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. It uses the same counting method on another group and shows that the number no longer comes out right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The logic of step 13 is to group cases of the same kind. But the משנה also has two cases of a cut or severed organ, which by that same logic should be counted as one. Doing so drops one place, so the total becomes seventeen instead of eighteen.

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If like cases are grouped together, the two severed cases must also be grouped, and that leaves the count one short of eighteen.

steps.title: The perforated spleen is itself a perforation
steps.stepSummary: A second challenge: רב עוירא's case in the name of רבא, the perforated spleen, is also a perforation. So it falls into the one 'perforation' slot and cannot fill one of the seven freed places.
steps.simpleTranslation: And also, the case of רב עוירא in the name of רבא is itself a perforation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second problem to the answer of step 13. One of the seven 'new' cases cannot really be counted as new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 counted every perforation as one item. The perforated spleen, one of the seven later cases from step 11, is also a perforation, so it is already inside that one item and cannot take an extra place. Together with step 14, the list is now two short of eighteen.
